sanskrit: kadambataruṣaṇḍaiś ca divyair mṛgagaṇair api divyaiḥ pakṣigaṇaiś caiva śuśubhe śvetaparvataḥ
english: With groves of kadamba trees and divine herds of deer, and with divine flocks of birds, the White Mountain shone with beauty.

sanskrit: tatra devagaṇāḥ sarve sarve caiva maharṣayaḥ meghatūryaravāś caiva kṣubdhodadhisamasvanāḥ
english: There all the hosts of gods and all the great sages gathered, along with the sounds of kettledrums like thunderclouds, roaring like a churned ocean.

sanskrit: tatra divyāś ca gandharvā nṛtyanty apsarasas tathā hṛṣṭānāṃ tatra bhūtānāṃ śrūyate ninado mahān
english: There the divine gandharvas danced, and the apsaras likewise; a great clamor was heard from the joyful beings assembled there.

sanskrit: evaṃ sendraṃ jagat sarvaṃ śvetaparvatasaṃsthitam prahṛṣṭaṃ prekṣate skandaṃ na ca glāyati darśanāt
english: Thus the entire world together with Indra, gathered on the White Mountain, gazed in delight upon Skanda and never wearied of beholding him.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca yadābhiṣikto bhagavān senāpatyena pāvakiḥ tadā saṃprasthitaḥ śrīmān hṛṣṭo bhadravaṭaṃ haraḥ rathenādityavarṇena pārvatyā sahitaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: When the blessed son of Fire had been consecrated as commander of the army, the glorious Hara, the lord, set out joyfully for Bhadravaṭa together with Pārvatī, riding a chariot radiant as the sun.

sanskrit: sahasraṃ tasya siṃhānāṃ tasmin yuktaṃ rathottame utpapāta divaṃ śubhraṃ kālenābhipracoditaḥ
english: A thousand lions were yoked to that best of chariots; propelled by time, it rose shining into the sky.

sanskrit: te pibanta ivākāśaṃ trāsayantaś carācarān siṃhā nabhasy agacchanta nadantaś cārukesarāḥ
english: Those lions, as if drinking in the sky and terrifying all moving and unmoving creatures, traveled through the heavens roaring, with their beautiful manes flowing.

sanskrit: tasmin rathe paśupatiḥ sthito bhāty umayā saha vidyutā sahitaḥ sūryaḥ sendracāpe ghane yathā
english: Standing in that chariot with Umā, the Lord of Beasts blazed forth like the sun accompanied by lightning within a cloud that bears Indra's rainbow.

sanskrit: agratas tasya bhagavān dhaneśo guhyakaiḥ saha āsthāya ruciraṃ yāti puṣpakaṃ naravāhanaḥ
english: Before him went the blessed lord of wealth, he who is borne by men, riding the lovely Puṣpaka chariot with his guhyaka attendants.

sanskrit: airāvataṃ samāsthāya śakraś cāpi suraiḥ saha pṛṣṭhato 'nuyayau yāntaṃ varadaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam
english: Mounting Airāvata, Śakra too followed behind with the gods, accompanying the granter of boons who bears the bull-banner.

sanskrit: jambhakair yakṣarakṣobhiḥ sragvibhiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ yāty amogho mahāyakṣo dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣam āsthitaḥ
english: Adorned with garlands, accompanied by jambhakas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, the mighty yakṣa Amogha proceeded, taking his position on the right flank.

sanskrit: tasya dakṣiṇato devā marutaś citrayodhinaḥ gacchanti vasubhiḥ sārdhaṃ rudraiś ca saha saṃgatāḥ
english: To his right went the gods, the Maruts who fight in varied ways, proceeding together with the Vasus and joined with the Rudras.

sanskrit: yamaś ca mṛtyunā sārdhaṃ sarvataḥ parivāritaḥ ghorair vyādhiśatair yāti ghorarūpavapus tathā
english: Yama too went, accompanied by Death, surrounded on all sides by hundreds of dreadful diseases, himself of terrible form and appearance.

sanskrit: yamasya pṛṣṭhataś caiva ghoras triśikharaḥ śitaḥ vijayo nāma rudrasya yāti śūlaḥ svalaṃkṛtaḥ
english: And behind Yama traveled Rudra's trident named Vijaya — dreadful, triple-peaked, sharp, and well adorned.

sanskrit: tam ugrapāśo varuṇo bhagavān salileśvaraḥ parivārya śanair yāti yādobhir vividhair vṛtaḥ
english: Behind it, Varuṇa, the blessed lord of waters, who wields the terrible noose, moved slowly, surrounded by diverse aquatic creatures.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato vijayasyāpi yāti rudrasya paṭṭiśaḥ gadāmusalaśaktyādyair vṛtaḥ praharaṇottamaiḥ
english: Behind the trident Vijaya also traveled Rudra's battleaxe, surrounded by the finest weapons — clubs, pestles, pikes, and others.

sanskrit: paṭṭiśaṃ tv anvagād rājaṃś chatraṃ raudraṃ mahāprabham kamaṇḍaluś cāpy anu taṃ maharṣigaṇasaṃvṛtaḥ
english: After the battleaxe followed, O king, the great-effulgent umbrella of Rudra, and after it the water-pot, surrounded by hosts of great sages.

sanskrit: tasya dakṣiṇato bhāti daṇḍo gacchañ śriyā vṛtaḥ bhṛgvaṅgirobhiḥ sahito devaiś cāpy abhipūjitaḥ
english: To his right the staff gleamed as it proceeded, clothed in splendor, accompanied by the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases, worshipped by the gods as well.

sanskrit: eṣāṃ tu pṛṣṭhato rudro vimale syandane sthitaḥ yāti saṃharṣayan sarvāṃs tejasā tridivaukasaḥ
english: Behind all of these Rudra traveled, standing in his spotless chariot, gladdening all the inhabitants of the three heavens with his radiance.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś caiva devāś ca gandharvā bhujagās tathā nadyo nadā drumāś caiva tathaivāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: Sages and gods, gandharvas and serpents, rivers and streams and trees, and likewise throngs of apsaras —

sanskrit: nakṣatrāṇi grahāś caiva devānāṃ śiśavaś ca ye striyaś ca vividhākārā yānti rudrasya pṛṣṭhataḥ sṛjantyaḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi cārurūpā varāṅganāḥ
english: — the nakṣatras and planets, and the children of the gods, and women of various forms — all followed in the wake of Rudra, and the lovely women of beautiful shape showered rains of flowers.

sanskrit: parjanyaś cāpy anuyayau namaskṛtya pinākinam chatraṃ tu pāṇḍuraṃ somas tasya mūrdhany adhārayat cāmare cāpi vāyuś ca gṛhītvāgniś ca viṣṭhitau
english: Parjanya too followed, having paid homage to the Bearer of the Bow; Soma held the white umbrella above his head; Wind and Fire took up the fly-whisks and stood in attendance.

sanskrit: śakraś ca pṛṣṭhatas tasya yāti rājañ śriyā vṛtaḥ saha rājarṣibhiḥ sarvaiḥ stuvāno vṛṣaketanam
english: And Śakra, O king, went behind him, clothed in splendor, together with all the royal sages, praising him who bears the bull-banner.

sanskrit: gaurī vidyātha gāndhārī keśinī mitrasāhvayā sāvitryā saha sarvās tāḥ pārvatyā yānti pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Gaurī, Vidyā, Gāndhārī, Keśinī, she called Mitra — all of them followed behind Pārvatī together with Sāvitrī.

sanskrit: tatra vidyāgaṇāḥ sarve ye ke cit kavibhiḥ kṛtāḥ yasya kurvanti vacanaṃ sendrā devāś camūmukhe
english: There all the hosts of sciences, whatever have been composed by the learned, whose word even the gods headed by Indra obey at the forefront of battle —

sanskrit: sa gṛhītvā patākāṃ tu yāty agre rākṣaso grahaḥ vyāpṛtas tu śmaśāne yo nityaṃ rudrasya vai sakhā piṅgalo nāma yakṣendro lokasyānandadāyakaḥ
english: — that rākṣasa planet, taking up a banner, went ahead; he who is ever busy in the cremation ground, indeed a friend of Rudra — the king of yakṣas named Piṅgala, the joy-giver of the world.

sanskrit: ebhiḥ sa sahitas tatra yayau devo yathāsukham agrataḥ pṛṣṭhataś caiva na hi tasya gatir dhruvā
english: Together with all these, the god traveled there at his ease, some going before and some behind — for his course of movement is not fixed.

sanskrit: rudraṃ satkarmabhir martyāḥ pūjayantīha daivatam śivam ity eva yaṃ prāhur īśaṃ rudraṃ pinākinam bhāvais tu vividhākāraiḥ pūjayanti maheśvaram
english: Mortals here worship Rudra the divine through righteous deeds, calling him Śiva, calling him Īśa, calling him Rudra, calling him the Bow-bearer; with devotion of all kinds they worship the Great Lord.

sanskrit: devasenāpatis tv evaṃ devasenābhir āvṛtaḥ anugacchati deveśaṃ brahmaṇyaḥ kṛttikāsutaḥ
english: Thus the divine army's commander, surrounded by the divine hosts, the son of the Kṛttikās who is devoted to the Brahman, followed the Lord of the Gods.

sanskrit: athābravīn mahāsenaṃ mahādevo bṛhadvacaḥ saptamaṃ mārutaskandhaṃ rakṣa nityam atandritaḥ
english: Then the Great God spoke a weighty word to Mahāsena: 'Guard the seventh atmospheric stratum without ever growing weary.'

sanskrit: skanda uvāca saptamaṃ mārutaskandhaṃ pālayiṣyāmy ahaṃ prabho yad anyad api me kāryaṃ deva tad vada māciram
english: Skanda said: I will guard the seventh atmospheric stratum, O lord. If there is any other task for me, O god, speak it without delay.

sanskrit: rudra uvāca kāryeṣv ahaṃ tvayā putra saṃdraṣṭavyaḥ sadaiva hi darśanān mama bhaktyā ca śreyaḥ param avāpsyasi
english: Rudra said: In matters of duty, O son, you must always look to me; for through seeing me and through devotion to me you will attain the highest good.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ity uktvā visasarjainaṃ pariṣvajya maheṣvaraḥ visarjite tataḥ skande babhūvautpātikaṃ mahat sahasaiva mahārāja devān sarvān pramohayat
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having spoken thus, the Great Lord embraced him and dismissed him. When Skanda was dismissed, there arose suddenly a great portent, O great king, which instantly threw all the gods into confusion.

sanskrit: jajvāla khaṃ sanakṣatraṃ pramūḍhaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhṛśam cacāla vyanadac corvī tamobhūtaṃ jagat prabho
english: The sky blazed up together with the nakṣatras; the world was utterly confounded; the earth quaked and cried out; the universe became filled with darkness, O lord.

sanskrit: tatas tad dāruṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣubhitaḥ śaṃkaras tadā umā caiva mahābhāgā devāś ca samaharṣayaḥ
english: Seeing that terrible sight, Śaṃkara became agitated, and so did the greatly blessed Umā and the gods together with the sages.

sanskrit: tatas teṣu pramūḍheṣu parvatāmbudasaṃnibham nānāpraharaṇaṃ ghoram adṛśyata mahad balam
english: While they were thrown into confusion, there appeared a vast and terrible army resembling mountains and storm-clouds, bearing weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: tad dhi ghoram asaṃkhyeyaṃ garjac ca vividhā giraḥ abhyadravad raṇe devān bhagavantaṃ ca śaṃkaram
english: That dreadful, innumerable host, roaring with manifold cries, rushed in battle upon the gods and upon the blessed Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: tair visṛṣṭāny anīkeṣu bāṇajālāny anekaśaḥ parvatāś ca śataghnyaś ca prāsāś ca parighā gadāḥ
english: By them were hurled into the ranks countless showers of arrows, and mountains, and śataghnis, and javelins, and iron bars, and clubs.

sanskrit: nipatadbhiś ca tair ghorair devānīkaṃ mahāyudhaiḥ kṣaṇena vyadravat sarvaṃ vimukhaṃ cāpy adṛśyata
english: Struck by those dreadful great weapons raining down, the divine army in an instant fled and was seen to have turned its face away.

sanskrit: nikṛttayodhanāgāśvaṃ kṛttāyudhamahāratham dānavair arditaṃ sainyaṃ devānāṃ vimukhaṃ babhau
english: The army of the gods, tormented by the dānavas, appeared to have turned away — its warrior-elephants and horses slain, its great chariot-warriors with weapons cut down.

sanskrit: asurair vadhyamānaṃ tat pāvakair iva kānanam apatad dagdhabhūyiṣṭhaṃ mahādrumavanaṃ yathā
english: Slaughtered by the asuras, it fell like a forest of great trees mostly burnt by fire.

sanskrit: te vibhinnaśirodehāḥ pracyavante divaukasaḥ na nātham adhyagacchanta vadhyamānā mahāraṇe
english: The celestials, their heads severed from their bodies, fell down; being slaughtered in that great battle, they found no protector.

sanskrit: atha tad vidrutaṃ sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvā devaḥ puraṃdaraḥ āśvāsayann uvācedaṃ balavad dānavārditam
english: Then the god Puraṃdara, seeing that powerful army routed and afflicted by the dānavas, encouraged it, speaking thus:

sanskrit: bhayaṃ tyajata bhadraṃ vaḥ śūrāḥ śastrāṇi gṛhṇata kurudhvaṃ vikrame buddhiṃ mā vaḥ kā cid vyathā bhavet
english: 'Abandon fear — blessings upon you! Take up your weapons, O heroes; set your minds on valor; let no distress come upon you.

sanskrit: jayatainān sudurvṛttān dānavān ghoradarśanān abhidravata bhadraṃ vo mayā saha mahāsurān
english: Conquer these utterly wicked, terrible-to-behold dānavas; attack these great asuras — blessings upon you — together with me!'

sanskrit: śakrasya vacanaṃ śrutvā samāśvastā divaukasaḥ dānavān pratyayudhyanta śakraṃ kṛtvā vyapāśrayam
english: Having heard Śakra's words, the celestials were reassured; they fought back against the dānavas, taking Śakra as their refuge.

sanskrit: tatas te tridaśāḥ sarve marutaś ca mahābalāḥ pratyudyayur mahāvegāḥ sādhyāś ca vasubhiḥ saha
english: Then all the thirty gods and the mighty Maruts advanced with great speed, as did the Sādhyas together with the Vasus.

sanskrit: tair visṛṣṭāny anīkeṣu kruddhaiḥ śastrāṇi saṃyuge śarāś ca daityakāyeṣu pibanti smāsṛgulbaṇam
english: The weapons discharged by them in their fury into the ranks in that battle, and the arrows too, drank the copious blood flowing from the bodies of the daityas.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dehān vinirbhidya śarās te niśitās tadā niṣpatanto adṛśyanta nagebhya iva pannagāḥ
english: Those sharp arrows, piercing through the bodies of the daityas, were then seen flying forth like serpents out of mountains.

sanskrit: tāni daityaśarīrāṇi nirbhinnāni sma sāyakaiḥ apatan bhūtale rājaṃś chinnābhrāṇīva sarvaśaḥ
english: Those bodies of the daityas, pierced through by the arrows, fell to the ground, O king, on every side like clouds that have been cut apart.

sanskrit: tatas tad dānavaṃ sainyaṃ sarvair devagaṇair yudhi trāsitaṃ vividhair bāṇaiḥ kṛtaṃ caiva parāṅmukham
english: Then that army of dānavas, terrified by all the hosts of gods in battle with various arrows, was made to turn its face away.

sanskrit: athotkruṣṭaṃ tadā hṛṣṭaiḥ sarvair devair udāyudhaiḥ saṃhatāni ca tūryāṇi tadā sarvāṇy anekaśaḥ
english: Then a great shout arose from all the joyful gods with weapons upraised, and all the various musical instruments sounded together in great numbers.

sanskrit: evam anyonyasaṃyuktaṃ yuddham āsīt sudāruṇam devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca māṃsaśoṇitakardamam
english: Thus the battle between the gods and the dānavas was utterly terrible, with flesh and blood for its mire, each side locked with the other.

sanskrit: anayo devalokasya sahasaiva vyadṛśyata tathā hi dānavā ghorā vinighnanti divaukasaḥ
english: Danger for the celestial world appeared suddenly, for the dreadful dānavas were slaying the celestials in such fashion.

sanskrit: tatas tūryapraṇādāś ca bherīṇāṃ ca mahāsvanāḥ babhūvur dānavendrāṇāṃ siṃhanādāś ca dāruṇāḥ
english: Then arose the blaring of instruments and the great sounds of kettledrums on the side of the dānava lords, and their dreadful lion-roars.

sanskrit: atha daityabalād ghorān niṣpapāta mahābalaḥ dānavo mahiṣo nāma pragṛhya vipulaṃ girim
english: Then from the terrible daitya forces there leapt forth a mighty dānava named Mahiṣa, seizing a great mountain.

sanskrit: te taṃ ghanair ivādityaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃparivāritam samudyatagiriṃ rājan vyadravanta divaukasaḥ
english: Seeing him surrounded like the sun by clouds, O king, with the mountain raised aloft, the celestials fled in terror.

sanskrit: athābhidrutya mahiṣo devāṃś cikṣepa taṃ girim patatā tena giriṇā devasainyasya pārthiva bhīmarūpeṇa nihatam ayutaṃ prāpatad bhuvi
english: Then Mahiṣa rushed upon the gods and hurled that mountain; struck by that terrible-formed falling mountain, O king, ten thousand of the divine army fell to the ground.

sanskrit: atha tair dānavaiḥ sārdhaṃ mahiṣas trāsayan surān abhyadravad raṇe tūrṇaṃ siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgān iva
english: Then Mahiṣa, together with those dānavas, terrifying the gods, charged swiftly in battle like a lion upon small deer.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ mahiṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā sendrā divaukasaḥ vyadravanta raṇe bhītā viśīrṇāyudhaketanāḥ
english: Seeing Mahiṣa bearing down, the celestials together with Indra fled in fear from the battle, their weapons and banners shattered.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa mahiṣaḥ kruddhas tūrṇaṃ rudrarathaṃ yayau abhidrutya ca jagrāha rudrasya rathakūbaram
english: Then that enraged Mahiṣa rushed swiftly toward Rudra's chariot, and rushing up he seized the pole of Rudra's chariot.

sanskrit: yadā rudrarathaṃ kruddho mahiṣaḥ sahasā gataḥ resatū rodasī gāḍhaṃ mumuhuś ca maharṣayaḥ
english: When the enraged Mahiṣa had swiftly reached Rudra's chariot, both earth and sky resounded mightily, and the great sages fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: vyanadaṃś ca mahākāyā daityā jaladharopamāḥ āsīc ca niścitaṃ teṣāṃ jitam asmābhir ity uta
english: The great-bodied daityas, resembling rain-clouds, roared aloud; and among them there was certainty: 'Victory is ours!'

sanskrit: tathābhūte tu bhagavān nāvadhīn mahiṣaṃ raṇe sasmāra ca tadā skandaṃ mṛtyuṃ tasya durātmanaḥ
english: Even in such a situation the blessed one did not slay Mahiṣa in battle, but rather he called to mind Skanda as the death of that evil-souled one.

sanskrit: mahiṣo 'pi rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā raudraṃ rudrasya nānadat devān saṃtrāsayaṃś cāpi daityāṃś cāpi praharṣayan
english: Mahiṣa too, having seized Rudra's dreadful chariot, roared repeatedly, terrifying the gods and delighting the daityas.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin bhaye ghore devānāṃ samupasthite ājagāma mahāsenaḥ krodhāt sūrya iva jvalan
english: Then, as that terrible danger for the gods arrived, Mahāsena came blazing with fury like the sun.

sanskrit: lohitāmbarasaṃvīto lohitasragvibhūṣaṇaḥ lohitāsyo mahābāhur hiraṇyakavacaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Clad in crimson garments, adorned with crimson garlands, crimson-faced, long-armed, wearing golden armor — the lord.

sanskrit: ratham ādityasaṃkāśam āsthitaḥ kanakaprabham taṃ dṛṣṭvā daityasenā sā vyadravat sahasā raṇe
english: Mounted on a chariot resembling the sun, radiant as gold — seeing him, that daitya army suddenly fled from the battle.

sanskrit: sa cāpi tāṃ prajvalitāṃ mahiṣasya vidāriṇīm mumoca śaktiṃ rājendra mahāseno mahābalaḥ
english: And mighty Mahāsena, O lord of kings, released that blazing śakti-spear that was the destroyer of Mahiṣa.

sanskrit: sā muktābhyahanac chaktir mahiṣasya śiro mahat papāta bhinne śirasi mahiṣas tyaktajīvitaḥ
english: Released, that śakti struck Mahiṣa's great head; when his head was split, Mahiṣa fell, his life departed.

sanskrit: kṣiptākṣiptā tu sā śaktir hatvā śatrūn sahasraśaḥ skandahastam anuprāptā dṛśyate devadānavaiḥ
english: That śakti, hurled once and hurled again, having slain enemies by the thousands, returned to Skanda's hand and was seen by gods and dānavas alike.

sanskrit: prāyaḥ śarair vinihatā mahāsenena dhīmatā śeṣā daityagaṇā ghorā bhītās trastā durāsadaiḥ skandasya pārṣadair hatvā bhakṣitāḥ śatasaṃghaśaḥ
english: The remaining hosts of terrible daityas, mostly struck down by the wise Mahāsena's arrows — frightened and terrified — were slain by Skanda's attendants, who are hard to withstand, and devoured in hundreds of groups.

sanskrit: dānavān bhakṣayantas te prapibantaś ca śoṇitam kṣaṇān nirdānavaṃ sarvam akārṣur bhṛśaharṣitāḥ
english: Devouring the dānavas and drinking their blood, those attendants in an instant made everything free of dānavas, exceedingly joyful.

sanskrit: tamāṃsīva yathā sūryo vṛkṣān agnir ghanān khagaḥ tathā skando 'jayac chatrūn svena vīryeṇa kīrtimān
english: As the sun conquers darkness, as fire conquers trees, as a bird conquers clouds, so Skanda the glorious conquered his enemies by his own valor.

sanskrit: saṃpūjyamānas tridaśair abhivādya maheśvaram śuśubhe kṛttikāputraḥ prakīrṇāṃśur ivāṃśumān
english: Worshipped by the thirty gods, having paid reverence to the Great Lord, the son of the Kṛttikās shone beautifully like the sun with its rays spread wide.

sanskrit: naṣṭaśatrur yadā skandaḥ prayātaś ca maheśvaram athābravīn mahāsenaṃ pariṣvajya puraṃdaraḥ
english: When Skanda, his enemy destroyed, went forward toward the Great Lord, Puraṃdara embraced Mahāsena and then spoke:

sanskrit: brahmadattavaraḥ skanda tvayāyaṃ mahiṣo hataḥ devās tṛṇamayā yasya babhūvur jayatāṃ vara so 'yaṃ tvayā mahābāho śamito devakaṇṭakaḥ
english: 'O Skanda, he who received boons from Brahmā — the Mahiṣa before whom the gods became as grass, the best among conquerors — that thorn in the side of the gods, O long-armed one, has been subdued by you.

sanskrit: śataṃ mahiṣatulyānāṃ dānavānāṃ tvayā raṇe nihataṃ devaśatrūṇāṃ yair vayaṃ pūrvatāpitāḥ
english: A hundred dānavas equal to Mahiṣa, enemies of the gods by whom we were previously tormented, have been slain by you in battle.

sanskrit: tāvakair bhakṣitāś cānye dānavāḥ śatasaṃghaśaḥ ajeyas tvaṃ raṇe 'rīṇām umāpatir iva prabhuḥ
english: And other dānavas have been devoured by your followers in hundreds of groups. You are unconquerable in battle by your enemies, like the lord, the husband of Umā.

sanskrit: etat te prathamaṃ deva khyātaṃ karma bhaviṣyati triṣu lokeṣu kīrtiś ca tavākṣayyā bhaviṣyati vaśagāś ca bhaviṣyanti surās tava surātmaja
english: This, O god, shall be proclaimed as your first deed of glory; your fame in the three worlds shall be imperishable; and the gods shall be under your sway, O son of the gods.'
